1.text: At Hochschule Mainz Support, the process starts when the Support Team receives a ticket and decides whether customer participation is required. If participation is needed, they contact the customer, who in turn provides details for the interview; using this input, the team conducts a detailed interview, then connects to the customer’s client and attempts to solve the problem together. After each attempt they assess whether further information is needed: if so, they ask the customer for more details and, once the customer provides the requested information, continue trying to solve the problem together; if no further information is needed, they create notes for documentation, send a ticket completion confirmation to the customer, and the process ends with the problem solved. If customer participation is not required, the Support Team solves the problem without the customer, then creates notes for documentation, sends the ticket completion confirmation to the customer, and the process ends with the problem solved. Communications between participants occur as follows: when the team contacts the customer, the customer provides interview details; when the team requests further information, the customer supplies it to enable continued problem solving; and when the team sends the completion confirmation, the customer receives it.

0.text: The process starts at SoKnow when the website is identified as outdated. The Marketing Department first analyzes the current content, after which the Development Department reviews the current content. From this review, two strands proceed at the same time: the Development Department designs new content, then updates the existing content, and finally permanently updates the content, after which the website is up-to-date; in parallel, the Marketing Department evaluates the content. If this evaluation is positive, management is informed and the work on that strand concludes with no improvements needed. If the evaluation is not positive, the work returns to reviewing the current content, which restarts the two parallel strands of development and evaluation; this cycle repeats until the evaluation is positive, at which point management is informed and that strand ends while the development strand reaches the updated website outcome after the permanent update.

If the applicant is suitable, the employment contract is sent to the applicant; once the signed contract is received, the process ends with the signed employment contract available.

Immediately afterward, three planning activities run in parallel: the doctor discusses the further course with the patient and relatives, the doctor determines medical care needs, and the nursing staff assesses nursing care needs. When all three are finished, the supply facility is defined. From there, two strands proceed in parallel: the doctor creates the doctor’s letter, and at the same time a decision is made on whether social services are required. If social services are required, social services initiate further care services, after which the discharge documentation is created; if they are not required, the discharge documentation is created directly. The doctor’s letter and the discharge documentation are then brought together, after which advanced discharge tasks are performed, and the process concludes with discharge completed.

0.text: The process begins in Request Fulfillment with the Incident Manager verifying the request. The Incident Manager then sends the order for request handling to 1st Level Support, where it is received and subsequently logged and categorized. Based on this, authorization is checked: if the request is not authorized, it returns to the Incident Manager for another verification; if authorized, four activities proceed in parallel. In parallel, the Incident Manager monitors and escalates the request, 1st Level Support monitors and escalates the request, the Service Request Fulfillment Group executes the request model, and 1st Level Support also executes the request model. Once all four parallel activities have completed, 1st Level Support performs request closure and evaluation. A check then determines whether there is any problem with processing or with the record: if there is no problem, Request Fulfillment Support provides request fulfillment support and the process ends successfully; if there is a problem, the Incident Manager is contacted about the problem and the process ends with the problem reported.

If it is not authorized, the flow returns to the Incident Manager to verify the request again. If it is authorized, the work splits into two paths that proceed in parallel: the Incident Manager monitors and, if needed, escalates the request, while the Service Request Fulfillment Group performs the request model execution. When both paths are completed, 1st Level Support proceeds with request closure and evaluation, followed by a check for any problem with processing or with the record. If the applicant is suitable, HR sends an invitation to the applicant and waits for the applicant’s response: if the invitation is declined, HR escalates the process and then archives the documents, ending the case as rejected; if the invitation is accepted, HR prepares and conducts an interview. Based on the interview, if the applicant is not good, HR rejects the applicant, sends the rejection notice, archives the documents, and the case ends as rejected. If the applicant is good, HR places the applicant on a list and makes a selection, after which the Board of Directors is asked to grant approval; if approval is not granted, HR rejects the applicant, sends the rejection notice, archives the documents, and the case ends as rejected. If approval is granted, HR confirms the applicant and prepares the contract, sending it to the applicant. The applicant then signs the contract, after which HR places the applicant in the position and occupies the position in the system, and the case ends with the applicant hired.

If the service is not found, the process ends immediately with the service not found. If the service is found, the client takes a ticket and indicates where it was taken. If it was taken in the app, the client waits for the indicated waiting time in the app, then uses the app to look for the product and specific criteria, and checks how many tickets are ahead; if it was taken physically, the client waits for their turn with the physical ticket. Both paths converge when the client’s turn is reached, at which point the client asks for the specific request, which is communicated to the store where the request is received. When the registration time is reached, the request is registered, and it is then assessed whether there are enough requests to respond to demand. If not enough, registration continues in a loop until there are enough. Once there are enough requests, an order request document is sent to the shop assistants team, who prepare the order and then deliver it to the client. The delivery is communicated to the client, who collects the order, and the process ends with the order collected.

0.text: The process starts in Accentis and an enquiry is created; this may be triggered by the customer submitting a sales enquiry. Depending on whether the situation is inbound or outbound, either a new contact is created or the existing enquiry is updated; these two paths rejoin before proceeding. The price and interest are then qualified, after which an approval request is sent to the customer. The customer reviews and provides their approval and a response is received back. Based on whether the price is approved, either the enquiry status is updated to not approved and the process ends with the enquiry not approved, or a quote is created. If a quote is created, a qualified requirements analysis is conducted, the enquiry status is updated, a job is created, and the process ends with the job created.

1.text: The process begins in Sales when a sales enquiry is on hand; the customer sends an enquiry, which Sales receives, and Sales records it as a new enquiry. Sales then determines whether the enquiry is inbound or outbound: for an inbound enquiry, a contact is created; for an outbound enquiry, the enquiry is updated instead. In either case, Sales proceeds to assess whether the price is acceptable and the customer is interested. Sales then sends a customer approval request to the customer; the customer receives this request, prepares a response, and sends the response back, which Sales receives. Based on the response, Sales decides whether the price is approved: if not approved, Sales updates the enquiry status to indicate the client is not approved and the process ends accordingly; if approved, Sales creates a quote, carries out a qualified requirements analysis, updates the enquiry status, creates a job, and the process ends with the job created.

0.text: The process starts with Program start in UI selection, after which the system starts the program for the player and asks whether to start a tutorial. If the tutorial is declined, the player proceeds with a standard key assignment and then chooses a menu option. If the tutorial is accepted, a tutorial on controller functions is run, after which the player is asked whether to start the game with the standard keys; accepting this proceeds directly to game start, while declining leads to choosing a menu option. When choosing a menu option, four paths are available: selecting Continue game resumes the game from the last end; selecting Load saved game retrieves saved game data and then continues from the saved point; selecting Start new game proceeds to game start; and selecting Game settings opens the game settings and then returns to choose a menu option again. From either resuming the game, continuing from a saved point, or proceeding to game start, the flow converges and audio setup begins with ambient noise generation and background music playback running concurrently and then synchronizing. Once audio is ready, the game is loaded, the system prompts for input, the player provides input, and the process ends when the game begins.

1.text: The process starts when the program is launched in the UI selection and the system starts the program for the player. The user is first asked whether to start a tutorial. If not, the standard key assignment is shown and the flow proceeds to the main menu. If yes, the controller tutorial runs; after the tutorial, the user is asked whether to start the game with the standard key assignment, and regardless of answering yes or choosing to return to the menu, the flow proceeds to the main menu. In the main menu, the user can choose among several options: selecting Settings opens the game settings and, after finishing there, returns to the main menu; choosing Continue game resumes the game from the last end and then proceeds to start the game; choosing Load saved game retrieves saved game data and then proceeds to start the game; choosing Start new game starts the game directly. Once the game starts, audio is prepared in parallel by generating ambient noise and playing background music; after both are ready, the game content is loaded, the user is prompted for input, gameplay begins, and the process ends.

At this point, a decision is made: if the answer is No, Standard key assignment is performed and then the flow proceeds to Show game menu (continue/load/new/settings); if the answer is Yes, Run controller tutorial is executed, after which the player is asked in Ask to start with standard key assignment, and regardless of whether the player answers Yes or No, the flow also proceeds to Show game menu (continue/load/new/settings). From the menu, a choice is made: if Continue game is selected, Resume game from last end is carried out and the process reaches Game begins; if Load saved game is selected, Retrieve saved game data is performed followed by Continue from saved point, and then the process reaches Game begins; if Start new game is selected, the flow splits so that Generate ambient noise and Play background music run in parallel, after which their results join to Load game, which then leads to Prompt user for input and finally to Game begins; if Game settings is selected, Access game settings is performed and control returns to the menu at Show game menu (continue/load/new/settings) for another choice. In all cases, the flow continues to displaying the menu options, the player selects a menu entry, and the following options apply: continuing the game resumes from the last save point; loading a saved game first retrieves saved data and then resumes from that point; starting a new game proceeds directly to a fresh start; choosing settings opens the game settings and then returns to the menu for another selection. From either resuming or starting a new game, the game setup begins by launching two preparations in parallel: ambient noise is generated while background music is played. Once both are ready, the game is loaded, the player is prompted for input, the player provides it, and the game begins.

0.text: The HR process starts with the HR department sending appointment suggestions. Immediately after that, the work splits into two parallel tracks: on one track, HR conducts the employee interview and then assigns training; on the other track, HR makes regular progress inquiries. The two tracks rejoin, after which HR waits to receive the employee’s training completion. Once that is received, HR marks the interview as conducted and the HR process ends. In the employee lane, the employee process starts independently, and the employee confirms the appointment, participates in the interview, completes the assigned training, and then the employee process ends. The following communications occur between the lanes: HR’s appointment suggestions are sent to the employee to enable the appointment confirmation; the employee’s confirmation is sent back to HR to proceed with the interview; after conducting the interview, HR notifies the employee to participate in it; once training is assigned by HR, that assignment is sent to the employee; HR’s regular progress inquiries are also sent to the employee while training is ongoing; and when the employee completes the training, a notification is sent to HR, which unblocks HR’s waiting point and allows the process to be closed.

Once these three strands have all finished—HR’s interview and training assignment, HR’s regular inquiries, and the employee’s confirmation, participation, and training completion—the process concludes with training completed and the interview conducted.

0.text: The process starts at the Library when a user logs in and their request is determined, after which one of three paths is taken based on the request type. If the request is to extend a medium, the extend-media procedure is initiated and a decision is made on the extension: when approved, the process ends with Media extension confirmed; when not approved, it ends with Medium returned. If the request is to borrow a medium, the user first selects the desired item and the system searches the database; if the item is available, the user is identified, the item is lent, and the process ends with Medium lent; if the item is not available, an unavailability notice is sent to the external user and the process ends with User notified of unavailability, with a corresponding message sent from the Library to the External User, who receives the unavailability message. If the request is to reserve a medium, a reservation decision is obtained: upon confirmation, the reservation is started and the process ends with Reservation completed; upon rejection, the lending is aborted and the process ends with Lending aborted.

1.text: The process starts when a user arrives at the library, logs in, and their request is determined. Based on the request type, one of three paths follows. If the request is to extend media, the media extension process is initiated; once that completes, a decision is made whether the extension is approved. If Yes, the process ends with the media extension confirmed; if No, the user returns the medium and the process ends with the medium returned. If the request is to borrow a medium, the user selects the desired medium and the system searches the database; if the medium is available, the user is identified, the medium is lent, and the process ends with the medium lent. If instead the medium is not available, an unavailability message is sent to a non-HTW user and the process ends with the unavailability message sent. If the request is to reserve a medium, a decision is taken whether the reservation is confirmed; if Yes, the reservation process is started and the process ends with the reservation started; if No, the lending process is aborted and the process ends with lending aborted.

2.text: The process starts when a user arrives at the library, after which the user is logged in and their request is determined. Based on the request, one of three paths is followed. If the user wants to extend a medium, the media extension process is initiated and a decision is made on whether the extension is approved. If approved, the process concludes with the media extension confirmed; if not, the user returns the medium and the process ends with the medium returned. If the user wants to borrow a medium, they first select the desired medium and it is searched in the database; depending on availability, either the user is identified and the medium is lent, ending with the medium lent, or, if it is not available, the non-HTW user is notified that the medium is unavailable and the process ends with the unavailability message sent. If the user wants to reserve a medium, the reservation request is reviewed and a decision is made; upon confirmation, the reservation process is started and the process ends with the reservation initiated, whereas a rejection leads to aborting the lending process and the process ends with the lending aborted.

3.text: The process starts when a user arrives at the library. The library logs the user in and determines what the user wants to do. If the request is to extend a loan, the library initiates the media extension process; if the extension is approved, the process ends with the media extension confirmed, otherwise the user must return the medium and the process ends once it has been returned. If the request is to borrow an item, the user selects the desired medium, the library searches the database for it, and, if it is available, the library identifies the user and lends the medium, ending with the medium lent; if it is not available, the library sends a not-available message to a non‑HTW user and the process ends with that message sent, and the user receives this not‑available message. If the request is instead a decision about proceeding with a loan, a choice is made: if the user opts to reserve, the reservation process is started and ends with the reservation initiated; if not, the lending is aborted and the process ends accordingly.

0.text: The process starts at the FMCG Company when the warehouse supervisor requests sample products from the supplier, sending a request to the supplier, who provides the sample products in response; the company then receives the sample. The warehouse supervisor evaluates the sample and, if it does not meet requirements, adjusts the product specifications and requests a new sample from the supplier, repeating this loop until a satisfactory sample is confirmed. Once the sample meets requirements, the warehouse supervisor selects the product and sends a purchase order to the supplier’s stock check. The supplier checks stock availability: if stock is insufficient, the supplier restocks inventory and rechecks until stock is available; once available, the supplier ships the product to the FMCG Company, which receives it. The warehouse supervisor inspects the received products and verifies whether the delivery matches the order. If anything is missing or incorrect, the warehouse supervisor requests the missing products from the supplier’s stock check, after which the supplier again checks availability (restocking and rechecking if needed) and ships the outstanding items back to the company; the company receives the additional delivery and inspects again, repeating this loop until the order and products match. When the delivery is correct and complete, the warehouse supervisor sends a payment authorization to Finance, which processes the payment, after which the company notifies the supplier of payment; the supplier receives this payment notification, and the process ends.

1.text: The process at the FMCG Company begins when the warehouse supervisor receives a sample request, then asks the supplier to provide sample products. This request triggers the supplier to provide the samples; once sent, the supplier informs the warehouse supervisor, who receives them and evaluates the sample. If the sample does not meet requirements, the warehouse supervisor adjusts the product specifications and requests new samples from the supplier, repeating the provide–evaluate cycle until the sample meets expectations. When the sample is acceptable, the warehouse supervisor selects the product and sends a purchase order to the supplier. On the supplier side, the purchase order is received, stock availability is checked, and if stock is available the supplier dispatches the product shipment to the warehouse supervisor; if stock is not available, the supplier restocks and rechecks availability until it can ship. The warehouse supervisor then receives the shipment and checks the products against the order. If they do not match, the warehouse supervisor requests the missing products from the supplier; the supplier receives this request, rechecks availability (restocking if needed), and sends the additional shipment, after which the warehouse supervisor receives it and checks again, repeating until the delivery matches the order. Once the order and products match, Finance sends a payment authorization, processes the payment, and notifies the supplier of the payment; the supplier acknowledges receipt of this notification, and the process concludes with the supplier having been notified.

The supplier provides the sample products and sends them back, after which the warehouse supervisor receives and evaluates them. If the samples meet requirements, the warehouse supervisor selects the product and sends a purchase order to the supplier, who checks stock availability. If the delivery matches the order, the warehouse supervisor sends a payment authorization to finance, which processes the payment and then notifies the supplier of the payment; the supplier acknowledges this, and the process completes. If the samples do not meet requirements, the warehouse supervisor adjusts the product specifications and requests new samples, repeating the evaluation cycle. If stock is not available when the order (or a later request) is received, the supplier restocks inventory and rechecks availability until it is available, then sends the product to the warehouse supervisor as before. If a received delivery does not match the order, the warehouse supervisor requests the missing products from the supplier, who checks stock availability (restocking if needed) and, once available, sends the missing products; the warehouse supervisor receives them and repeats the check against the order before proceeding to payment as described.

On receiving the purchase order, the supplier checks stock availability: if available, the supplier sends the product; if not, the supplier restocks inventory and rechecks availability until it is available, then sends the product. The warehouse supervisor receives the product and checks it against the order. If the delivered products match the order, the warehouse supervisor sends a payment authorization, the payment is processed, and the supplier is notified of the payment; the FMCG Company process then ends. In parallel with that final step, the supplier receives the payment notification and their process ends. If the delivered products do not match the order, the warehouse supervisor requests the missing products from the supplier, which triggers another stock-availability check on the supplier side (with restocking if required) and another product delivery to the FMCG Company, after which the receipt and verification steps are repeated until the delivery matches the order.

9.text: When a sample request is received at the FMCG company, the warehouse supervisor requests sample products from the supplier, who then provides them; the FMCG team receives the samples and evaluates them. If the sample meets requirements, the warehouse supervisor selects the product and sends a purchase order to the supplier; otherwise, the specifications are adjusted and a new sample request is issued, repeating the evaluation loop. Upon receiving the purchase order, the supplier checks stock availability: if stock is available, the supplier sends the product to the FMCG company; if not, the supplier restocks inventory and rechecks availability until the product can be sent. The FMCG warehouse supervisor receives the delivered product and inspects it. If the delivery matches the order, the warehouse supervisor sends a payment authorization to Finance, which processes the payment and notifies the supplier of payment; the process concludes once the supplier has been notified. If the delivery does not match the order, the warehouse supervisor requests the missing products from the supplier, prompting the supplier to recheck stock availability (restocking as needed) and send the missing items; once received, the FMCG team repeats receipt and inspection, and only when the delivery matches the order does the process continue to payment and supplier notification. Throughout, the following communications occur: the initial sample request is sent to the supplier and the supplied samples are sent back; the purchase order is sent to the supplier to trigger stock checking and fulfillment; shipping notifications correspond to the supplier sending products to FMCG; any request for missing items is sent back to the supplier to trigger another stock check and shipment; and, after payment is processed, the supplier receives the payment notification.

0.text: The process begins when the customer starts and fills a credit application, then sends it to the mediation agency. The mediation agency receives the application and simultaneously forwards it to Bank A and Bank B. At Bank A, the request is received and the loan amount is checked against 20 times the applicant’s income: if it exceeds this threshold, a rejection is sent back to the mediation agency; otherwise, an interest of 20% per year is estimated and a credit report is sent back. At Bank B, the request is received and the applicant’s income is checked: if it is not between €2,000 and €100,000, a rejection is sent back; if it is within that range, the loan amount is then checked against 20 times the monthly income: if it exceeds this threshold, a rejection is sent; otherwise, an interest rate is determined and a credit report is sent back. The mediation agency waits until responses from both banks arrive, consolidates them, and decides whether any credit proposal is available: if at least one proposal exists, a credit proposal is sent to the customer, who receives it and the process completes with the credit proposal outcome; if no proposal is available (both responses are rejections), a rejection is sent to the customer, who receives it and the process completes with the rejection outcome.

1.text: The process starts with the customer, who fills the credit application and then sends it to the mediation agency; this submission is received by the agency. The agency immediately proceeds to handle both banks in parallel: it sends a loan request to Bank A and another to Bank B. At Bank A, upon receiving the loan request, the bank checks the loan amount and decides whether the requested amount is greater than 20 times the income; if so, it sends a rejection to the mediation agency and completes its processing, otherwise it estimates a 20% annual interest and sends a credit report to the mediation agency, then completes. At Bank B, upon receiving the loan request, the bank checks whether the income is between €2,000 and €100,000; if not, it sends a rejection to the mediation agency and completes. If the income is in range, it checks the loan amount against the income and decides whether the requested amount is greater than 20 times the income; if so, it sends a rejection to the mediation agency and completes, otherwise it determines the interest rate and sends a credit report to the mediation agency, then completes. The mediation agency waits until both responses have been received in parallel (one from Bank A and one from Bank B), then forwards the collected responses to the customer, completing its part. The customer receives the bank responses and the overall loan process completes. Communications between participants occur as follows: the customer’s application is sent to and received by the mediation agency; the agency’s loan requests are sent respectively to and received by Bank A and Bank B; Bank A’s rejection or credit report is sent back to and received by the agency; Bank B’s rejection or credit report is sent back to and received by the agency; and finally, the agency forwards both banks’ responses to and is received by the customer.

2.text: The process starts when the customer begins and fills out a credit application, then sends it to the mediation agency. The mediation agency receives the application and immediately splits the case to approach both Bank A and Bank B in parallel: it forwards the request to Bank A and to Bank B, each bank receiving the request. At Bank A, the request is checked for the relationship between loan amount and income; if the amount is greater than twenty times the income, a rejection is sent back to the mediation agency, otherwise an offer is prepared by estimating 20% interest per year and sending a credit report to the mediation agency. At Bank B, the bank first verifies whether the income lies between €2,000 and €100,000; if it is outside this range, a rejection is sent to the mediation agency. If the income is within range, Bank B then checks whether the loan amount exceeds twenty times the monthly income; if it does, a rejection is sent, otherwise the interest rate is determined and a credit report is sent to the mediation agency. The mediation agency receives Bank A’s response (either rejection or credit report) and separately receives Bank B’s response, waits until both have arrived, and then forwards the combined responses to the customer. The customer receives the decision (either rejections or one or more credit proposals), and the process completes.

In parallel, Bank B receives the loan request, first verifies whether the applicant’s income is within €2,000–€100,000, and sends a rejection if it is not; if it is, Bank B then checks whether the requested amount exceeds 20 times the monthly income, sending a rejection if it does, or determining an interest rate and sending a credit report if it does not. The mediation agency receives the responses from both banks, waits until both have arrived, and then forwards the combined results to the customer. The customer receives the outcome and, depending on what was returned, the process ends either with the loan being rejected or with a credit proposal received.

0.text: The process starts in Purchasing by obtaining and reviewing offers; based on whether the offer exceeds €2000, either the offer is approved first (if Yes, > €2000) or the ordering proceeds directly (if No, ≤ €2000). In both cases, the next step is to order the goods. After ordering, Purchasing monitors whether the delivery is on time. If it is not on time, a new delivery deadline is set and the timeliness is checked again, repeating until the delivery is on time. Once on time, Purchasing performs the final acceptance of the goods and sends the goods to Goods Receipt. Goods Receipt then inspects the delivery and decides whether it is complete. If the delivery is complete, Goods Receipt confirms the delivery, after which Accounting/Controlling initiates payment and forwards it internally, and the process ends with office supplies purchased. If the delivery is not complete, Purchasing contacts the supplier and requests a new delivery, after which the process returns to checking whether the delivery is on time, continuing as before until the delivery arrives on time and complete.

Once on time, the goods are finally accepted and sent to goods receipt, where the delivery is inspected. If the delivery is complete, the delivery is confirmed, payment is initiated, and then forwarded to Accounting/Controlling, who process the payment, after which the process concludes with the office supplies purchased. If the delivery is incomplete, the supplier is contacted and a new delivery is requested; the supplier schedules a new delivery, and the process returns to checking whether delivery is on time.

This description is communicated to the consultation team, who identify the problem and find a solution, then describe the solution to the customer. The customer applies the solution, after which it is assessed whether the solution is helpful. If yes, the customer implements the solution and the process ends with the problem resolved. If no, the customer requests a new solution, which is sent to the consultation team; they propose a new solution back to the customer, who applies the new solution and then assesses whether this new solution is helpful. If the new solution is helpful, the customer implements the solution and the process ends with the problem resolved. If it is still not helpful, the consultation team suggests further solutions and the process ends with the problem resolved. Throughout, the following communications take place: the problem description is sent from the customer to the consultation team; the proposed solution is sent from the consultation team to the customer for application; a request for a new solution is sent from the customer to the consultation team; and the new solution proposal is sent from the consultation team to the customer for application.

This exchange repeats until a helpful solution is found, after which the customer implements it and the process concludes with the problem resolved.

0.text: When a booking request is received in the taxi system, a customer service operator checks the user data. If the data is incomplete, the taxi system sends a cancellation to the customer due to missing data, which the customer receives, and the process ends with the booking cancelled. If the data is complete, the operator checks available cars and the taxi system evaluates whether one can arrive within 30 minutes. If no car can make it in that time, the taxi system sends a cancellation to the customer due to lack of cars, which the customer receives, and the process ends with the booking cancelled. If a car is available within 30 minutes, the taxi system displays a list of options, the operator selects the nearest car together with the client, the taxi system calculates the time of arrival, the operator books the taxi, and the taxi system sends the booking confirmation to the customer, which the customer receives, after which the process ends with the booking confirmed.

1.text: When a Booking request received arrives in the Taxi System, the Customer Service Operator checks user data. If the data is incomplete, the Taxi System sends cancellation message to customer, which the Customer receives as Receive cancellation message, and the process ends as Booking cancelled. If the data is complete, the Operator checks available cars and the Taxi System evaluates car availability (next 30 minutes). If no cars are available in the next 30 minutes, the Taxi System sends cancellation message to customer, the Customer receives it as Receive cancellation message, and the process ends as Booking cancelled. If cars are available, the Taxi System displays list of options, the Operator picks nearest car with client, the Taxi System calculates time of arrival, and the Operator books taxi. The Taxi System then sends booking confirmation to customer, which the Customer receives as Receive booking confirmation, and the process finishes with Booking confirmed.

2.text: The process starts when the customer submits a booking request, which is received by the taxi booking company. The customer service operator checks the user data and decides whether the data is complete. If the answer is “No, data incomplete,” a cancellation message is sent to the customer and the process ends with the booking cancelled. If the answer is “Yes, data complete,” the operator checks for available cars and evaluates whether a car is available within 30 minutes. If the answer is “No, not available,” a cancellation message is sent to the customer and the process ends with the booking cancelled. If the answer is “Yes, available,” the system displays a list of options, the operator and client pick the nearest car, the system calculates the time of arrival, and the operator books the taxi. The system then sends a booking confirmation to the customer and the process ends with the booking confirmed. The communications that occur are: the customer’s booking request is sent to the company at the start, a cancellation message is sent to the customer in either of the two negative cases, and a booking confirmation is sent to the customer upon successful booking.

The operator checks the user data, after which a decision is made on whether the data are complete. If the data are incomplete, a cancellation message is sent to the customer and the process ends with the booking cancelled; the customer receives this cancellation. If the data are complete, the operator checks whether a car is available within the next 30 minutes. If no car is available in that timeframe, a cancellation message is sent to the customer and the process ends with the booking cancelled; the customer receives this cancellation. If a car is available, the system displays a list of options, the operator selects the nearest car together with the client, the system calculates the time of arrival, and the operator books the taxi. A booking confirmation is then sent to the customer, who receives it, and the process ends with the booking confirmed.

4.text: When a booking request is received by the Taxi Booking Service, a customer service operator checks the provided data. If none is available in that timeframe, the Taxi System sends a cancellation to the customer indicating no cars are available, and the process ends with the booking cancelled for that reason. If a car is available, the Taxi System displays a list of options to the operator, who then picks the nearest car together with the client. The Taxi System calculates the time of arrival, after which the operator books the taxi and the Taxi System sends a booking confirmation to the customer. The process concludes with the booking confirmed. Throughout the process, the customer receives a cancellation message when a cancellation is sent and receives a booking confirmation when a booking is confirmed.

0.text: The process at ACME AG starts in the Department, where parts availability is checked. If the parts are in stock, the Department retrieves the parts from storage and the process ends with the parts retrieved from storage. If the parts are not in stock, the Department specifies and quantifies the requirements and then completes a purchase order. Central Purchasing then checks the purchase order and determines whether the vendor is known. If the vendor is known, an order template is created from the purchase order; if the vendor is not known, a new vendor is created first and then the order template is created. The Approver then approves the purchase order, after which Central Purchasing records the receipt of goods. At that point, if there are delivery problems, the order status is adjusted and the process ends with the order cancelled due to delivery issues; otherwise, the process ends with the parts procured.

0.text: The process starts with the applicant and begins when the start signal triggers the creation of the application. The applicant then sends the application to the loan provider, who receives it and checks whether the document is complete. If it is complete, the loan provider accepts the document and the process ends with “Providing completed.” If it is not complete, the loan provider returns the document to the applicant, who completes the missing information and sends it back. Upon receiving this resubmission, the loan provider admits the document and the process ends again with “Providing completed.”

1.text: The process starts simultaneously for both parties: the applicant begins by creating the application while, on the lender’s side, the provider opens the process to receive it. Once created, the application is sent by the applicant to the loan provider, who then receives it and checks whether the documents are complete. If everything is in order, the provider accepts the document and the provision is completed. If something is missing, the provider returns the submission to the applicant for completion. The applicant receives this return, completes the missing information, and sends the completed information back. The provider waits until the completed information is received, then admits the document, and the provision is completed.

2.text: The process starts with the applicant creating an application. The application is then sent to the loan provider, who receives it and checks the document for completeness. If the document is complete, the loan provider accepts the document and the process moves toward its conclusion. If the document is incomplete, the loan provider returns the application to the applicant for completion. The applicant completes the missing information and sends the updated document back to the loan provider, who then admits the document. After either accepting the complete document directly or admitting it after completion, the flow converges and the process ends with providing completed.

3.text: The process starts when the applicant creates the application, after which the loan provider receives it and checks whether the document set is complete. If it is complete, the loan provider accepts the document and the procedure ends with providing completed. If it is not complete, the loan provider returns it to the applicant to complete the missing information; the applicant then provides the missing information and sends it back, upon which the loan provider admits the document and the procedure ends with providing finished.

4.text: The process begins with the applicant, who starts by creating the application; once created, this results in the application being submitted. This submission is communicated to the loan provider, who, upon receiving the application, begins their work by registering it and checking the document for completeness. If the document is complete, the loan provider accepts the document and finishes with providing completed. If the document is incomplete, the loan provider returns the application to the applicant and pauses with returned to applicant (wait). That return is communicated to the applicant, who then starts their follow-up by completing the missing information and finishes with the application resubmitted. This resubmission is communicated back to the loan provider, who then starts the subsequent handling by admitting the document and finishes with providing finished.

If the outcome is incomplete, Loan Processing performs Return to applicant for completion and sends the request back to the Applicant. The applicant then performs Complete missing information and sends the completed information to the Loan Provider, where Loan Processing continues with Admit document, after which the process ends with Providing finished.

0.text: The process starts in the HR Department, where HR secures personnel development needs (initial) and then analyzes employee data. Based on this, three activities proceed in parallel: HR checks personnel capacity, determines capacity requirements, and identifies training opportunities. Once all three are completed, HR conducts an employee interview. After the interview, three further activities run in parallel: HR considers a training request, considers improvement suggestions, and allocates training. When these have all been completed, HR discusses the outcome with the department head. HR then organizes training and continuing education, updates the competency profile, and secures personnel development needs (final), after which the process ends.

0.text: The process starts in the Development Department with order intake, followed by describing the requirements, conducting a workshop, and creating a project sketch. After the sketch is created, the team waits until an appointment confirmation is received from the Customer Company; this confirmation is provided by the customer and triggers the next step. The team then conducts a customer conversation and writes a specification sheet, which is sent to the customer for review. The customer reviews the specification sheet and provides feedback back to the team, after which the team performs project and capacity planning, checks standard open-source products, defines use cases, and calculates costs. A decision is then made: if existing products can be used, the team adjusts the knowledge management systems in line with the target process; if new products must be developed, the team develops a new product as the target process. Both paths rejoin and lead to product acceptance with the customer, during which the customer participates. The team then obtains post-acceptance feedback provided by the customer, identifies follow-up projects, completes the order, and the process ends.

Depending on whether a new product needs to be developed, the team either adjusts the knowledge management systems as a target process or develops a new product as a target process; regardless of the chosen approach, the work then converges and proceeds to product acceptance. 0.text: The process starts at the seller, who first displays items on the webpage. A buyer then purchases an item, which triggers the seller to receive the buyer’s order and immediately send an order confirmation back to the buyer; the buyer receives this confirmation. The seller forwards the order to the shipping company, which prepares the item for shipment and then checks whether delivery succeeds. If delivery succeeds, the shipping company delivers the item to the customer and informs the eBay platform, which tracks the order and notifies the buyer to close it; the buyer closes the order and the process ends with the order closed. If delivery does not occur, the shipping company notifies the buyer of the non-delivery, upon which the buyer chooses a resolution: either reimbursement or reshipment. For reimbursement, the buyer sends a reimbursement request to the seller; once the seller receives this decision, the seller reimburses the money to the buyer and the process ends on the seller side with an escalation end. For reshipment, the buyer sends a reshipment request to the seller; after receiving this decision, the seller sends the order again to the shipping company, which repeats preparation and the delivery check, either leading to successful delivery and order closure via eBay as before, or another non-delivery notification that brings the buyer back to choose between reimbursement and reshipment again. Throughout, the communications are: buyer to seller for the initial order, seller to buyer for the confirmation, seller to shipping to initiate shipment, shipping to eBay upon delivery, eBay to buyer to close the order, shipping to buyer upon non-delivery, and buyer to seller for either reimbursement or reshipment decisions.

1.text: The seller begins by launching the process and displaying items on the webpage, which are made available to the buyer. The buyer, while browsing, decides to purchase an item and sends the purchase to the seller, who receives the order, sends a purchase confirmation back to the buyer, and forwards the order to the shipping company. The shipping company receives the order from the seller, obtains the item, and then determines whether delivery is successful. If delivery succeeds, the item is delivered to the customer, and the shipping company reports the delivery to eBay, which tracks the order and notifies the buyer that the order is ready to close; the buyer then closes the order and the process ends. If delivery does not succeed, the shipping company notifies the buyer of a non-delivery; the buyer chooses how to resolve the issue by either requesting a reimbursement or a reshipment and sends the chosen request to the seller. Upon receiving the buyer’s decision, the seller either reimburses the buyer—after which the process ends with a reimbursement escalation—or resends the order to the shipping company, which repeats the shipping steps as before.

2.text: The process starts at the seller, who displays items on the webpage and thereby prompts the buyer to purchase an item. The buyer places the purchase, which is received by the seller; the seller then sends an order purchase confirmation to the buyer and forwards the order to the shipping company. The shipping company receives the order, obtains the item, and determines the delivery outcome: if successful, the item is delivered to the customer, which triggers eBay to track the order and send a tracking update to the buyer; upon receiving this update, the buyer closes the order and the process ends with the order closed. If the outcome is non-delivery, the shipping company notifies the buyer, who then decides either to request a money reimbursement or a reshipment of the item. If the buyer requests reimbursement, the request is sent to the seller, who processes the reimbursement and the process ends for the seller with the order reimbursed. If the buyer requests a reshipment, the request reaches the seller, who sends the order again to the shipping company, after which the shipping steps and decision on delivery outcome repeat as before.

3.text: The online selling process starts on the marketplace, which triggers the seller to display items on a webpage and makes them available to the buyer; the buyer then purchases an item, and that purchase is sent to the seller, who receives the buyer’s order. The seller responds by sending a purchase confirmation, which the buyer receives, and forwards the order to the shipping company, which in turn picks the item. Once the item is ready, the shipping company evaluates whether it was delivered. If it was delivered, the shipping company hands the item to the customer, and this handover is reported to the marketplace to track the order, after which the marketplace informs the buyer so the buyer can close the order and the process ends with the order closed. If it was not delivered, the shipping company notifies the buyer of the non-delivery; the buyer then decides on a resolution. If the buyer chooses reimbursement, the buyer requests reimbursement from the seller, which triggers the seller to reimburse the money, and the process ends with the refund processed. If the buyer chooses reshipment, the buyer requests a reshipment from the seller, which sends the order again to the shipping company; the shipping company picks the item again and the delivery decision is repeated as before. Communications between participants occur throughout: the seller’s item display leads to the buyer’s purchase; the buyer’s purchase reaches the seller as an order; the seller’s confirmation reaches the buyer; the seller’s order to ship reaches the shipping company, which triggers picking the item; the delivery handover is reported to the marketplace for tracking, which then informs the buyer to close the order; a non-delivery notice reaches the buyer to trigger the resolution decision; a reimbursement request from the buyer triggers the seller’s reimbursement; and a reshipment request from the buyer triggers sending a new order to the shipping company.

4.text: At the Seller, the process starts and items are displayed on the webpage. The Buyer sees these items and purchases one, which prompts the Seller to receive the buyer’s order, send a purchase confirmation to the Buyer, and then forward the order to the Shipping Company. Upon receiving the order, the Shipping Company gets the item and determines whether it can be delivered. If delivery succeeds, the item is delivered to the customer, and eBay is notified to track the order; eBay then informs the Buyer, who closes the order and the process ends. If delivery does not occur, the Shipping Company notifies the Seller of the non-delivery, and the Buyer is asked to decide the next step: either request a reimbursement or request a reshipment. If the Buyer requests a reimbursement, the Seller receives the reimbursement request, reimburses the money, and the process ends with a reimbursement escalation. If the Buyer requests a reshipment, the Seller receives the reshipment request and resends the order to the Shipping Company, which again gets the item and repeats the delivery decision and follow-up as before. Communications between participants occur as follows: the Seller’s display leads the Buyer to purchase; the Buyer’s purchase triggers the Seller’s receipt of order; the Seller’s purchase confirmation reaches the Buyer; the order sent by the Seller reaches the Shipping Company to get the item; successful delivery is reported to eBay, which then informs the Buyer to close the order; non-delivery is reported by the Shipping Company to the Buyer to decide the next step; a reimbursement request from the Buyer reaches the Seller; and a reshipment request from the Buyer reaches the Seller.

5.text: The process starts at the seller when the process is started and items are displayed on the webpage. The buyer then purchases an item, which sends the order to the seller. The seller receives the buyer’s order, confirms it to the buyer, and forwards the order to the shipping company. The shipping company receives the order and gets the item ready for shipment, assesses whether delivery is on time, and proceeds to deliver the item to the customer; the outcome of this assessment is communicated to the buyer, prompting the buyer to decide between requesting a refund or a reshipment. After delivery, the shipping company notifies the platform, which tracks the order and then passes it on to the buyer to close; the buyer closes the order and the process ends with the order closed. If the buyer chooses a refund, the buyer requests money reimbursement, the seller receives this decision and reimburses the money, and the process ends on the seller side with a refund escalation. If instead the buyer requests a reshipment, the buyer sends that request to the seller, who sends the order again to the shipping company, which repeats the shipment and delivery cycle as before.

6.text: At the seller, the process starts when it is initiated and items are displayed on the webpage; in parallel, the buyer starts and purchases an item, which sends an order to the seller who receives the buyer order. The seller then sends a purchase confirmation, which the buyer receives, and forwards the order to the shipping company; this dispatch is received by the shipping company, which gets the item and decides whether it can be delivered. If delivery is possible, the item is delivered to the customer and a delivery notification is sent to the eBay platform, which tracks the order and then notifies the buyer to close the order, after which the buyer closes it and the process ends with the order closed. If delivery is not possible, the shipping company sends a non-delivery notice that the buyer receives, prompting a buyer decision between requesting money reimbursement or requesting reshipment; either request is sent as a decision to the seller, who then receives the buyer decision, records it, and routes accordingly: when a reimbursement is requested, the seller reimburses the money and the process ends on the seller side with refund completed; when a reshipment is requested, the seller again sends the order to the shipping company, which repeats the receive–get item–deliver or notify non-delivery path as before.

7.text: The online selling process starts at the seller, who first displays items on the webpage. A buyer then purchases an item, sending the order to the seller, who receives it and sends a purchase confirmation back to the buyer. The seller forwards the order to the shipping company, which retrieves the item and determines the delivery status. If the item is delivered to the customer, tracking is performed by eBay, which then notifies the buyer to close the order; the buyer closes it and the process ends with the order closed. If the item is not delivered, the shipping company notifies the buyer of the non-delivery. The buyer then decides whether to seek reimbursement or a reshipment: if reimbursement is requested, the request is sent to the seller, who reimburses the money, and the process ends with a refund escalation; if a reshipment is requested, the buyer sends that request to the seller, who sends the order again to the shipping company, after which the shipping company again retrieves the item and checks delivery status as before.

8.text: The process starts at the seller when items are displayed on the webpage. A buyer then purchases an item and sends the order to the seller, who receives the buyer’s order and responds by sending a purchase confirmation to the buyer, where it is received. The seller forwards the order to the shipping company, which prompts the shipper to get the item and decide whether it can be delivered. If delivery proceeds, the shipper delivers the item to the customer and notifies the tracking service, which in turn informs the buyer so the buyer can close the order, ending the process with the order closed. If delivery cannot be completed, the shipper reports the non-delivery to the buyer, where the notice is received and a resolution is chosen: the buyer either requests reimbursement or requests a reshipment. A reimbursement request is sent to the seller, who receives it, reimburses the money, and the process ends via the escalation end. A reshipment request is sent to the seller, who receives it and again sends the order to the shipping company, restarting the shipping sequence (get item and decide on delivery): if this delivery succeeds, tracking informs the buyer and the buyer closes the order; if it fails again, the buyer receives another non-delivery notice and chooses once more between reimbursement and another reshipment.

9.text: The process starts at the seller when the items are displayed on the webpage. This prompts the buyer to purchase an item, upon which the buyer’s order is sent to the seller. The seller receives the order, sends a purchase confirmation back to the buyer, and then forwards the order to the shipping company. The shipping company retrieves the item and determines whether delivery can be completed. If the item is delivered, it is handed over to the customer, which triggers a notification to the eBay tracking service; eBay in turn informs the buyer, who then closes the order and the process ends with the order closed. If delivery does not occur, a notification is raised for the buyer, who decides what to do in case of non-delivery and communicates that decision to the seller. The seller receives the buyer’s decision and either reimburses the money, after which the process ends via the escalation end, or sends the order again to the shipping company, returning to the shipping steps for another delivery attempt. Throughout, the key communications are: items shown by the seller to the buyer, the buyer’s order sent to the seller, the purchase confirmation sent back to the buyer, the handover of the order from the seller to the shipper, the delivery status sent from the shipper to the buyer for decision when not delivered, the buyer’s decision sent to the seller, the delivery notification sent from the shipper to eBay, and the tracking update sent from eBay to the buyer to close the order.

0.text: The process starts in the Development Department with order intake, followed by purchasing the knowledge management system. The development team then receives the customer’s initial adjustment requests, which the customer sends, and proceeds to make the adjustments. After completing them, the team notifies the customer that the adjustments are completed, and then finds a test group, conducts tests, and evaluates the results. If the results are not positive, the team returns to making adjustments and repeats notification and testing. If the results are positive, the team conducts workshops with the test group, trains employees, and then awaits any post-training adjustment requests from the customer; if such requests arrive, the team returns to making adjustments, otherwise it informs the customer that the product is finished. Independently, after completing adjustments, the team can also proceed directly to inform the customer that the product is finished. After informing the customer, a decision is made on whether the adjustments are satisfactory; if not, the team again returns to making adjustments, otherwise it implements the knowledge management system and completes the order. Throughout, the customer communicates by sending the initial adjustment requests that trigger the team’s receipt, receiving the notification that adjustments are completed, optionally sending post-training adjustment requests to the team, and upon receiving the “product finished” notice, performing their own verification of whether the adjustments are satisfactory.

1.text: After order intake in the Development Department, the team purchases the knowledge management system and then waits for the customer to provide initial adjustment requests, which are received and used to make the first round of adjustments. The team then notifies the customer about the adjustments. Next, they search for a suitable test group, requesting participants from the Test Group, and conduct tests with those participants. The results are evaluated; if the results are not positive, further adjustments are made and the tests are repeated until the results are positive. Once the results are positive, the team conducts workshops with the test group and then trains employees. Afterward, they wait for any post-workshop adjustment requests from the customer; if such requests arrive, they make the requested adjustments and then inform the customer that the product is finished. If no post-workshop requests arrive, they inform the customer directly that the product is finished. The customer, upon receiving this information, reviews whether the adjustments are satisfactory and then sends a satisfaction decision back to Development. If the decision indicates that the adjustments are not satisfactory, Development makes additional adjustments and again informs the customer that the product is finished, after which the customer re-evaluates and resubmits a decision; this cycle repeats until the decision confirms that the adjustments are satisfactory. Once the adjustments are confirmed as satisfactory, the Development Department implements the knowledge management system and completes the order. Communications in this process include: the customer providing initial adjustment requests to Development; Development notifying the customer about adjustments; Development requesting test group participants from the Test Group; the customer providing post-workshop adjustment requests to Development when applicable; Development informing the customer that the product is finished; the customer internally checking satisfaction and sending the resulting decision to Development.

2.text: The process starts in the development department with order intake, followed by purchasing the knowledge management system. Development then awaits and receives the customer’s initial adjustment requests, which the customer provides. Based on these, development makes the initial adjustments and notifies the customer. Development searches for a suitable test group, conducts tests, and evaluates the test results. If the results are not positive, development returns to making adjustments and immediately repeats the tests without performing a new search for a test group, iterating until the results are positive. Once the results are positive, development conducts test group workshops and then trains employees. After training, development waits for post-workshop adjustment requests; the customer, having received the notification from development, prepares and sends these requests, which development receives. If such requests are present, development makes the post‑workshop adjustments; if not, it proceeds directly to inform the customer that the product is finished. In both cases, development informs the customer that the product is finished, after which the customer receives this information, reviews the product, and sends satisfaction feedback, which development receives. If the feedback indicates the adjustments are not yet satisfactory, development returns to making the post‑workshop adjustments and repeats informing the customer and receiving feedback until the feedback is satisfactory. Once the adjustments are satisfactory, development implements the knowledge management system and the order is completed. Communications between the organizations occur when the customer provides the initial adjustment requests to development, when development notifies the customer after the initial adjustments, when the customer sends post‑workshop adjustment requests back to development, when development informs the customer that the product is finished, and when the customer sends satisfaction feedback to development.

The team then receives the customer’s initial adjustment requests (provided by the customer) and makes the initial adjustments. Afterward, development awaits any later adjustment requests from the customer; if the customer provides such requests, they are received and additional adjustments are made. If they are not, the customer submits later adjustment requests, which development receives and processes as described, iterating until the customer is satisfied. Once the customer confirms satisfaction, this confirmation is received by development, which then implements the knowledge management system and completes the order.

7.text: The process starts with order intake in the development department, after which the team purchases the knowledge management system. They then await and receive the customer’s initial adjustment requests, apply the initial adjustments, and notify the customer that these adjustments are completed (sending a notification to the customer). Next, they find a test group, run tests, and evaluate the test results. If the results are not positive, they make further adjustments and run another round of tests, returning to the evaluation and repeating this cycle until the results are positive. Once the results are positive, they conduct workshops with the test group, train employees, and then receive any post‑training adjustment requests from the customer. If such requests are present, they make the post‑training adjustments; if no requests are present, they proceed directly to informing the customer that the product is finished and send the finished‑product information. They then receive the customer’s validation result and decide whether the adjustments are satisfactory. If the validation is negative, they return to make post‑training adjustments and then inform the customer again, leading back to a new validation cycle. If the validation is positive, they implement the knowledge management system and complete the order. Communication with the customer occurs at three points: the customer sends the initial and post‑training adjustment requests to the development team, the team notifies the customer when initial and final work is completed, and the customer sends the final validation result back to the team.
